history.content: Python 3.13 added an experimental free-threaded build, a new interactive REPL, and an experimental JIT compiler.

candidates.title: Pi - Wikipedia
candidates.snippet: The number π (/ paɪ / ⓘ; spelled out as pi) is a mathematical constant, approximately equal to 3.14159, that is the ratio of a circle 's circumference to its diameter. It appears in many formulae across mathematics and physics, and some of these formulae are commonly used for defining π, to avoid relying on the definition of the length of a curve. The number π is an irrational number ...

candidates.title: Pi Day - Wikipedia
candidates.snippet: Pi Day is observed on March 14 (the 3rd month) since 3, 1, and 4 are the first three significant figures of π ${\displaystyle \pi }$ and was founded in 1988 by Larry Shaw, an employee of the Exploratorium, a science museum in San Francisco. [2][3] Celebrations often involve eating pie or holding pi recitation competitions.

candidates.title: What Is Pi Day? | Date, Origin, Albert Einstein, & Pie | Britannica
candidates.snippet: The numerical value of pi to five decimal places is 3.14159; hence, Pi Day is celebrated on March 14 (3/14). Pi Day is often celebrated with pies or pizzas decorated with the Greek letter π. American physicist Larry Shaw, who worked at the Exploratorium, a science museum in San Francisco, devised the holiday at a staff retreat in 1988.

candidates.title: What's new in Python 3.14 — Python 3.15.2 documentation
candidates.snippet: Summary - Release highlights ¶ Python 3.14 is a stable release of the Python programming language, with a mix of changes to the language, the implementation, and the standard library. The biggest changes include template string literals, deferred evaluation of annotations, and support for subinterpreters in the standard library.
